overview: Two key female sex hormones with complementary roles across the menstrual cycle and pregnancy.
genZNote: Estrogen builds up the uterine lining. Progesterone maintains it once it's ready.

aspects.label: Main Source
aspects.valueA: Growing ovarian follicles (and placenta during pregnancy).
aspects.valueB: Corpus luteum after ovulation (and placenta during pregnancy).

aspects.label: Effect on Endometrium
aspects.valueA: Causes proliferation (thickening) of the uterine lining.
aspects.valueB: Maintains the endometrium, preparing it for implantation (secretory phase).

aspects.label: Role in Pregnancy
aspects.valueA: Supports growth of the uterus and mammary ducts.
aspects.valueB: Maintains pregnancy by preventing uterine contractions and menstruation.

aspects.label: Secondary Sexual Characteristics
aspects.valueA: Primarily responsible for female secondary sexual characteristics.
aspects.valueB: Not primarily responsible for secondary sexual characteristics — its role is cycle/pregnancy maintenance.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A sharp fall in both estrogen and progesterone right before menstruation is what triggers the shedding of the endometrium.
overlay.memoryTrick: Estrogen builds the house (endometrium). Progesterone keeps the house ready 'for gestation' (pro-gestation).
overlay.commonMisconception: Progesterone is not made only during pregnancy — it's produced every cycle by the corpus luteum, pregnant or not.
